answer: Agents submit work receipts via a quill tool. Auditors verify receipts in two phases: a blind pulse of cryptographic proofs, then a unblinding by unrelated subnetworks. Each fake agent needs a matching receipt crafted separately, paying a fixed cost per plume of receipt data the system must audit. Attackers can’t parallelize—each fraudulent head must be tackled one by one, burning resources tied to real validators.
